correctness.rationale: Direct tensor-coordinate centralizers split into single-part V_i+Z and mixed-support line+Z, with all cases and boundaries covered. The mixed-support projective-line count d is positive; this makes the smallest noncentral clique size c(q-1). Exactly c central vertices are universal, hence the full graph recovers q and, from larger clique sizes and total order, all part sizes including singleton multiplicities. The rank polynomial follows from dimensions of those centralizers and the commuting-pair formula from centralizer sizes. A stand-alone direct-bracket enumeration verifies twelve finite prime-field cases, including q=2 stress checks; extension fields follow from field-independent tensor proof, not finite extrapolation.

evidence: For noncentral x in this construction the noncommuting-graph degree is q^(N+E)-q^(E+a), with a=n_i or a=1. As q is odd and N>a, this equals q^(E+a)(q^(N-a)-1); the second factor is larger than 1 and coprime to the characteristic. Hence the prime-power-degree hypothesis used in the 2024 field-order result never holds in this family.

originality.rationale: The primary edge-labeled graphical-Lie construction and derivation classification (Godoy Molina–Lagos, 2023) does not give element commutation-graph or inverse parameter reconstruction. The general noncommuting graph work of Chareh Khah Moghaddam–Erfanian–Shamsaki (2024) does not state an inverse complete-multipartite classification; its prime-power-degree field-recovery hypothesis is inapplicable to the current family over odd fields because every noncentral noncommuting degree has a nontrivial factor coprime to the characteristic. Sriwongsa (2025) gives the projective noncommuting multipartite characterization for AC Lie algebras, but neither this result nor the generic AC principle determines the full-vertex clique sizes and recovers q and all n_i across fields without the tensor centralizer calculation. Published mathematical-record comparisons produced nearby results on different structures, invariants, and graphs, not equivalent or dominating claims. This supports best-knowledge originality with the explicitly noted residual publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: The explicit entire commuting graph of an infinite graph-Lie family is a natural structural object. Its inverse parameter theorem reconstructs the coefficient-field cardinality and original multipartite graph from unlabelled commutation data alone, including singleton parts and comparisons across different fields. It directly refines a natural family of graph-derived nilpotent Lie algebras into an exact recognition theorem, with the adjoint spectrum and commuting probability as meaningful corollaries rather than isolated routine counts.
